# Vendored shadPS4

These files come from [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4), licensed GPL-2.0 (see `LICENSE`).

- **Commit:** `14ada48a1320` ("vk_rasterizer: Apply pending fast clears on FMASK decompress (#5283)")
- **Paths:** `src/common`, `src/video_core`, `src/shader_recompiler`, `LICENSE`
- **Imported with:** `python scripts/import_shadps4.py --src ../shadps4 --commit 14ada48`

`sotcgpu` (`gpu/`) builds these sources. It replaces what they take from shadPS4's `core/` with shim headers
under `gpu/shim/`.

## Local patches

Local patches are allowed: M4's AjncSystem fixes will be patches on this copy. Every patch must be listed
below: the file, what changed, and why. Re-running `import_shadps4.py` drops them, so re-apply them
afterwards.

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `src/video_core/amdgpu/liverpool.h`, `liverpool.cpp` | `SubmitGfx`/`SubmitAsc` take an optional `Common::UniqueFunction<void> on_done` (default empty). `GpuQueue` keeps one callback per submission (`submit_done_cbs`, pushed with the task); `Process()` pops it with the finished task and runs it on the GPU thread, outside the queue lock. | `sotcgpu_submit_gfx`/`_compute` promise a `done` callback once the command processor has consumed the buffers (the runtime advances compute ring read pointers with it). Liverpool had no completion hook. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp` | `Draw`, `DrawIndirect`, `DispatchDirect` and `DispatchIndirect` return early when `SotcSkipPipeline(pipeline)` (from `gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h`) is true. | Debug switch `SOTC_GPU_SKIP=<hash>[,<hash>...]`: drop the draws of one shader to bisect GPU hangs and rendering bugs. Inactive when the variable is unset. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp` | In `Presenter::Present`, `#ifdef SOTC_NO_IMGUI`: the "Draw the game" ImGui block and `ImGui::Core::Render` are replaced by a plain fitted blit of the frame into the swapchain image (clear to black, `MakeImageBlitFit`, layouts restored to what the rest of `Present` expects). Without the define the file is unchanged. | shadPS4 draws the game frame as an ImGui image; sotcgpu compiles ImGui out (no imgui submodule, no src/imgui sources). |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp` | `ObtainBuffer` streams a small read-only buffer only when the region is CPU-modified, and adds it to a new `streamed_ranges` set. Otherwise it binds the buffer in place from the arena. `TickFrame` calls the new `FlushStreamedRanges`, which uploads those ranges to the arena (`EnsureResident` + `SynchronizeMemory`, split at arena pages and 64 MiB). | SotC binds ~85k small read-only buffers per frame (~330 MiB). Streaming all of them each bind wrapped the 128 MiB stream buffer several times a frame, and each wrap waited for the GPU. The title ran at 4 flips/s with 1.3 GiB/s of guest copies; with the patch, copies fall to ~50 MiB/s and the title runs at 8–20 flips/s. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp` | Includes `sotc_debug.h` (`gpu/src/`). `Draw` and `DrawIndirect` call `SotcDebug::OnDraw(indirect, texture_cache, cb_descs, state.num_color_attachments, db_desc)` right after `BeginRendering`; `DispatchDirect`/`DispatchIndirect` call `SotcDebug::Count(Counter::Dispatch)`. | Workstream X debug tools (`gpu/src/debug_dump.cpp`): `SOTC_DUMP_RT` records the targets each draw binds, `SOTC_GPU_STATS` counts draws and dispatches. One relaxed load and a branch while the variables are unset. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp` | Includes `sotc_debug.h`. `Scheduler::Wait` counts a blocking wait (`!IsFree(tick)`) when `SotcDebug::StatsEnabled()`. | `SOTC_GPU_STATS`: blocking scheduler waits per second. The `IsFree` check only runs while stats are on. |
| `src/video_core/cache_storage.cpp` | Loose-file mode writes each blob to `<name>.tmp` and renames it into place. `Close()` runs the requests still queued after stopping the IO thread. `num_requests` is `std::atomic<u32>`. | sotcgpu enables the on-disk pipeline cache (P1), and `smoke.py` kills the game: a blob cut short mid-write would make the next start's `WarmUp` assert. Queued writes were dropped at shutdown. The counter was decremented without the lock, so a lost update could leave the IO thread spinning. |
| `src/video_core/amdgpu/pm4_cmds.h`, `liverpool.cpp` | New packet structs `PM4CmdSetPredication` (GFX6-8 layout: address lo, then address bits 39:32, `draw_visible` bit 8, `hint` bit 12, `pred_op` bits 18:16, `continue` bit 31) and `PM4CmdGetLodStats` (best-guess layout). In `ProcessGraphics`: `IT_SET_PREDICATION` tracks the active predication (until `pred_op = Clear`) and logs its fields; every type-3 packet first goes through `SotcPredicationSkips`, which drops it per `SOTC_PRED=run|skip|skipall|eval` (default `run` = shadPS4 behaviour, nothing dropped). `IT_GET_LOD_STATS` writes zeros (at most 4 KiB) to its destination when that is a GPU mapping (`SOTC_LOD_STATS=off` disables the write) and logs its raw dwords. All state is file-static on the GPU thread. | shadPS4 ignored both packets ("Unimplemented"). Workstream Q (`docs/next/q.md`): find out whether SotC uses predication, and experiment with skipping predicated draws for the DOF squares (#4) and flashing shapes. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | Both `Vulkan::Check` overloads take a defaulted `std::source_location` and, on failure, call `SotcDiag::CheckFailed`, which logs one `[vkcheck]` line (result name, caller file/line/function, a hint for DeviceLost / OutOfDeviceMemory / TooManyObjects) and then the `[vram]` report, before the unchanged assert. Adds `namespace Vulkan::SotcDiag`: atomic counters and the `report` hook that sotcgpu installs. | Workstream C (`docs/next/c.md`): the ~230 s crash only said `vk_platform.h:66 Check: Assertion Failed!`, with no caller and no memory state. Diagnostic only. |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp` (`EnsureResident`), `buffer.cpp` (`UniqueBuffer::Create`), `texture_cache/image.cpp` (`UniqueImage`) | Count sparse-arena residency (bytes and `vkAllocateMemory` calls), sparse arena buffers, and live VMA images (count, bytes from `vmaGetAllocationInfo`) in `SotcDiag`. On a failed `allocateMemory` / sparse `createBuffer` / `vmaCreateBuffer` / `vmaCreateImage`, log a `[vram] ... failed` line with the request (size, address range, image extent/format) before the existing assert. | Same: VRAM budget diagnostics. No behavior change. |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/residency_allocator.h`, `residency_allocator.cpp` (new), `buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | Opt-in: `SOTC_RESIDENCY=chunks`. The default (`legacy`) keeps shadPS4's one `vkAllocateMemory` per `EnsureResident` call, because chunks stalled or crashed in 2 of 3 intro runs. New `VideoCore::ResidencyAllocator`: 256 MiB device-memory chunks (dedicated chunk when a request is larger) carved into block-granular slices; best fit, else free ranges largest-first (at most 16 slices), else a new chunk; `Free` and `ReleaseEmptyChunks` for eviction. Vulkan-free core with injected allocate/free callbacks. `EnsureResident` allocates its gaps from it and emits one sparse bind + one `Backing` per gap/slice piece instead of one `vkAllocateMemory` per call. `~BufferCache` waits for the device to go idle; the chunks are freed after the arenas. `SotcDiag` gains `arena_chunks`/`arena_chunk_bytes`; `arena_resident_bytes`/`arena_allocations` now mean bytes in slices / chunk allocations (`PublishResidencyStats`). | Workstream R part 1 (`docs/next/r.md`): the ~230 s `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` came after 1,700–2,400 residency allocations against NVIDIA's `maxMemoryAllocationCount` of 4096. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_residency.cpp`. |
| `src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`, `texture_cache.cpp`, `sotc_gc_policy.h` (new) | `GarbageCollectImages` is rewritten around `VideoCore::SotcGc` (Vulkan-free, header-only). Thresholds are 50/70/85 % of `Instance::GetTotalMemoryBudget()` (normal/pressured/critical; idle below). One pass per tick walks the LRU oldest first. Images whose guest bytes are current go after 120/30/8 ticks unused. **Tiled GPU-written images (`SafeToDownload`) go without a download** after 1800/300/60 ticks. Linear GPU-written ones are downloaded, then freed, under pressure (as before). At most 8/32/128 frees and 4096 visits per tick; kept images no longer use up the free budget. Totals go to `SotcDiag::gc_*`. New `SotcPublishImageBreakdown` (every ~10 s, GPU thread) writes `SotcDiag::gc_breakdown`: live images by age bucket, targets / texture-only / tiled GPU-written, images sharing a base address, view count, the 4 largest. shadPS4's threshold members are still computed but no longer used for images. | Workstream T (`docs/next/t.md`): VRAM grew past the 6 GB card's budget (1,392 live images, 3.8 GiB at 580 s). shadPS4 never freed tiled GPU-written images (every render and depth target). It also counted them against the per-tick deletion budget, so a few at the LRU head stopped the GC for good, and its trigger is 0 on cards under 8 GB. Freeing without a download doesn't change what the CPU sees: tiled images are never written back to guest memory. A re-created image uploads the guest bytes. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_gc_policy.cpp`. |
| `src/common/lru_cache.h` | `ForEachItemBelow`: `RETURNS_BOOL` tests `std::invoke_result_t<Func, ObjectType&>` instead of the `std::invoke_result<...>` struct. | It was always false, so a callback's `return true` never stopped the walk (image and sampler GC). Workstream T. |
| `src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/flatten_extended_userdata_pass.cpp` | `PushPtr` emits a null guard in the SRT walker: a pointer below 0x10000 (after the 48-bit mask) is replaced by a 64 KiB static zero block, so that walk reads zeros. `SrtWalkerSignalHandler` stays as the fallback. | SotC leaves some SRT pointers 0 in its first frames. The walker faulted and the handler patched the load to `xor reg,reg` **for good**, so those shaders kept reading zeros after the game filled the pointers in: an intermittent black screen from boot on (in the log: ~488 `Patched SRT walker ... fault address 0x8..0x860` lines at ~2 s). Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_recompiler.cpp` (`TestSrtWalkerNullPointer`). |
| `src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`, `texture_cache.cpp`, `sotc_gc_policy.h` | Working-set diagnostics appended to the `[vram] images:` line (`| working set: ...`): images used in the last 8 ticks, distinct images touched per GC tick (`TouchImage` counts the first touch per tick; last and max), guest bytes summed vs. unique (`SotcGc::AnalyzeOverlap`), images overlapping another live image (and how many are CPU-dirty), and images created at an address the GC freed within 60 ticks (`SotcGc::RefaultTracker`). | Session 5 (`docs/NEXT.md`): in critical mode every image is "unused <60 ticks" because the GC frees anything older. These counters tell a real working set from duplicated copies of reused guest memory or GC thrash. Diagnostic only. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_gc_policy.cpp`. |
| `src/video_core/texture_cache/image.h`, `image.cpp` | New `Image::SotcAllocatedBytes()` (VMA size of all backing images) and `Image::SotcViewCount()`. | Workstream T `[vram] images:` breakdown. Diagnostic only. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | `SotcDiag` gains `gc_level`, `gc_freed`, `gc_freed_stale`, `gc_downloaded`, `gc_skipped` and the mutex-guarded string `gc_breakdown` (includes `<mutex>`, `<string>`). | Workstream T: sotcgpu's `[vram]` line prints the image GC level and totals, followed by an `[vram] images:` line with the breakdown. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h`, `vk_rasterizer.cpp` | New `Rasterizer::SotcGcTick()` (just `texture_cache.RunGarbageCollector()`), called by sotcgpu on every flip (`SubmitFlipInternal`, GPU thread). | shadPS4 runs the image GC only from `OnSubmit`, which needs every queue drained. During SotC's cinematics and gameplay the next frame is always queued (and the game stops calling `sceGnmSubmitDone` after the logos), so the GC ran about once in 2 s at best and VRAM ran out at the gameplay load. |
| `src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`, `texture_cache.cpp`, `sotc_gc_policy.h`, `image.cpp`, `buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | Emergency image GC. On `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` in `EnsureResident` (legacy `allocateMemory` or the chunk allocator) or in `UniqueImage::Create` (`vmaCreateImage`, through the `SotcDiag::emergency_gc` hook the texture cache installs), `TextureCache::SotcEmergencyCollect` frees images not used in this GC tick, oldest first (`SotcGc::Level::Emergency`: age >= 1, GPU-written tiled images too, no downloads), until `EmergencyTarget(request)` = max(2x request, 256 MiB). Images `FindImage` is resolving are pinned (`sotc_gc_pinned`). It runs only on the GC thread and never nested. Then `scheduler.Finish()` + `PopPendingOperations()` so the frees reach the driver. The caller retries once and asserts only if that fails. Counters `gc_emergency_*`. **Images use `VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT`.** `BufferCache::SotcPublishArenaCoverage` (called with the image breakdown) publishes `arena_ranges_bytes`/`arena_image_bytes`: arena resident bytes inside live images' guest ranges (`SotcGc::IntersectBytes`, `AnalyzeOverlap`'s new `unions` output). | Session 5 (`docs/NEXT.md`): VRAM exhaustion asserted. With VMA's shared blocks a freed image only left a hole: the first emergency pass freed 259 MiB, device usage didn't move, and the retry failed. Dedicated allocations return the memory immediately and cut steady-state heap0 usage below the budget (no emergency pass needed in a 370 s gameplay run). Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_gc_policy.cpp`. |

When a patch changes the SPIR-V that `shader_recompiler` generates, bump `kPipelineCacheVersion` in
`gpu/src/sotcgpu.cpp`. The pipeline cache only checks shadPS4's own version numbers, so without the bump it
would keep loading shaders compiled before the patch.

Everything else shadPS4 takes from its `core/`, `imgui/`, Tracy and Abseil is replaced by headers under
`gpu/shim/` (see `docs/m3/gl.md`), not by edits here. `common/logging/log.cpp` and `common/path_util.cpp` are
not compiled; `gpu/src/log.cpp` and `gpu/src/path_util.cpp` replace them.
